newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Protesting judges have decided to stop wearing black and pin their hope on parliament's support for their demand to place the administrative court under the judiciary. The resolution is made public in a statement issued by the "working group on administrative court for the people" on the last day of a two-day seminar attended by some 2,000 judges nationwide. (BANGKOK POST)

- Two refugee camps in Tha Song Yang and Phop Phra districts in Tak province caught fire over the weekend causing over 500 Karen refugees to live without shelter. Sources in the Karen National Union say the fire incidents took place a day after Thai soldiers and border patrol police had searched for weapons at the camps. A new refugee camp will be built in Umphang district, Tak, to serve 6,500 Karen refugees who had just fled several bases overrun by Burmese government troops earlier this month. (BANGKOK POST)

- Lack of qualified rural teachers is threatening the ambitious plan for long-distance education for students in remote areas, and the satellite equipment provided is being used by unsupervised locals to tune in to other television programmes. The problem underlined the main stumbling block of Thailand's education reform. (THE NATION) + + + +

- The prime minister has told various agencies to collect economic data to counter a threat by Moody's Investor Service to review Thailand's credit worthiness and downgrade the country's debt rating. General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says Thailand needs to explain to Moody's directly that although the country is experiencing economic problems it is still capable of regaining economic strength. Moody's team of analysts will be in Thailand on March 6 and 7 and are scheduled to meet with the finance minister, the Bank of Thailand governor, and other top officials. (BANGKOK POST) (BUSINESS DAY)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has approved in principle Thai Airways International's proposal to replace president Thamnoon Wanglee as part of a policy to rotate senior airline executives to improve its management. An airline source says Chavalit has even approached Veerachai Vannikkul, former managing director of the now-defunct Air Siam who also held senior management posts at the Bangkok Bank and Bangkok Metropolitan Bank, to replace Thamnoon. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Association of Thai Steel Industries is petitioning the government to exempt billet from import duties in a bid to defend its position against moves by other steel producers. The association says the government is planning to increase the duty on billet from the current 5 percent to 12.5 percent, in favour of steel producers which have blast furnaces. (BUSINESS DAY)
